entries.title: The Cat Lady

emulation.notes: Use the native Windows release for capture; Linux users can use Proton.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Native 2D PC presentation with modern display/capture flexibility.

primary.why: The Windows PC release is the best current fidelity/capture route for The Cat Lady; the native Linux build existed but has been pulled and has no sourced content advantage.
primary.how_to_play: Buy The Cat Lady on Steam or GOG and play the Windows PC build. On Linux handhelds/desktops, prefer the Windows build through Proton rather than chasing the removed native Linux build.

all_releases.fidelity: Original native PC release with current storefront availability and PC capture flexibility.
all_releases.reason: primary: active/current PC route with no sourced content loss versus Linux.

all_releases.fidelity: Native Linux build released after Windows, but it was later pulled.
all_releases.reason: skip: no unique content advantage, and the removed native build is a worse current recommendation than Windows/Proton.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: No sourced platform-exclusive content split was identified.

entries.remaster_caveats: Original release; no remake/remaster distinction applies. The native Linux build was later pulled, so Windows is the stable current route.

entries.title: Downfall

emulation.notes: Use the native Windows remake for the main run; no emulator is needed.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Native 2016 PC remake presentation with PC capture flexibility.

primary.why: The 2016 Windows remake is the best primary route because it was reworked from the ground up with new script, graphics, music, mechanics, and The Cat Lady-style presentation while the package still includes the original 2009 version for comparison.
primary.how_to_play: Buy Downfall on Steam and play the 2016 remake as the main run. Then launch the included original 2009 point-and-click version only if you want the original-version differences.

secondary.exclusive_content: Original 2009 point-and-click version included with the Steam release/freeware, with different original presentation and historical content from the 2016 rework.
secondary.what_to_play: Play the included 2009 original after the remake only for historical/original-version comparison.
secondary.why: The remake is higher fidelity and more complete as the modern primary, but the original is materially different and included.

all_releases.fidelity: Original Adventure Game Studio point-and-click release; now included/freeware but unsupported in the Steam package.
all_releases.reason: secondary: historically distinct original version with different presentation, but lower fidelity than the 2016 remake.

all_releases.fidelity: Ground-up 2016 remake with reworked graphics, music, mechanics, and modern PC storefront support.
all_releases.reason: primary: highest fidelity and best current package, while the original 2009 version remains included for completeness.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: The 2016 remake is the highest-fidelity and current primary route, but the original 2009 point-and-click version is materially different and is included/freeware; use the original as a secondary historical pass only.

entries.remaster_caveats: The 2016 version is a remake rather than a simple remaster: the script, graphics, music, and mechanics were reworked from the ground up. The original 2009 version is included but unsupported.

entries.title: Lorelai

emulation.notes: Use the native PC release for capture.

primary.why: The Windows PC release is the only sourced release route and is the best fidelity/capture path for Lorelai's full-HD trilogy finale.
primary.how_to_play: Buy Lorelai on Steam and play the Windows PC build as the primary route.

all_releases.reason: primary: only sourced platform route and best capture/fidelity option.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: No sourced platform-exclusive content split was identified.

entries.remaster_caveats: Original release; no remake/remaster distinction applies.
